title: Grateful Dead Live at Kiel Auditorium on 1973-10-30
lineage: Dat (Sony D8) -> RME Hammerfall Digiface -> Sony Vaio C1VP ->
source: SBD -> Master Reel (7inch Master Reels @ 7.5ips 1/2trk) -> DCassette (Tascam 122mkIII) -> Dat (Panasonic 3700/44.1k) D

ai_review.summary: High‑quality soundboard capture of a mellow 1973 show, highlighted by a soaring Here Comes Sunshine and jazzy Dark Star/Mind Left Body sequence.
ai_review.review: The Miller‑remastered SBD delivers clear, well‑balanced guitars and keyboards with only occasional tape‑noise quirks, while the band offers a relaxed, space‑filled performance. Standout moments include a radiant Here Comes Sunshine, an extended Dark Star → Mind Left Body jam, and superb renditions of Eyes of the World and Playing in the Band; the first set feels tighter than the second, which drifts into a dreamy, jazz‑inflected vibe.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews are 4–5 stars praising both performance and sound; only a few note minor technical flaws or slower tempos, yielding an overall strong consensus.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑balanced mix with clear guitars and keys. Reviewers mention occasional high‑pitched tape “kettle” noise on the Miller source, a slightly over‑driven bass and minor vocal tuning issues, but overall the SBD is listenable and enjoyable.

standout_songs: Dark Star > Mind Left Body > Dark Star
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is tight and energetic, building nicely into a spacey second set that leans toward jazzy, relaxed improvisation. The transition from Dark Star through MLB to Eyes of the World forms the centerpiece, followed by a mellow winding‑down to the encore.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s leads are praised as hot, melodic and harmonically rich (especially on Dark Star/MLB), though he was slightly out of tune on Looks Like Rain.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh’s bass is noted as deep and booming; highlighted for strong presence in the Dark Star intro and MLB jam, but occasionally over‑driven.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s rhythm work and vocals receive mixed notes – solid rhythm on Jack Straw and Row Jimmy, but three‑part vocal blend was a bit off on Looks Like Rain. Guitar contributions later in the set are described as interesting and supportive.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s organ/keyboard is lauded for jazzy big‑band textures, strong comping throughout, occasional repetitive riff toward the end of Eyes, and overall balance with guitars.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drumming is generally described as steady and appropriate to the relaxed vibe; no specific criticisms noted.
